name: Horn of Echeyakee
summary: At the Crossroads, Sergra Darkthorn gives hunters the Horn of Echeyakee. Sounded among the ancient kodo remains northeast of the settlement, it calls the legendary white predator of the Barrens.

sections.title: Calling the Whitemist
sections.body: Hunters who are being tested in the hunt receive the horn. Its call summons Echeyakee, whose name means “Whitemist” in Taur-ahe. Tauren hunters revere the king of the savannah cats as both mercy and death. He strikes so swiftly that his quarry feels neither terror nor suffering. The horn belongs at the predator’s lair, among giant kodo bones behind the hills northeast of the Crossroads.

faq.q: What does the Horn of Echeyakee do?
aliases: what is horn of echeyakee for
faq.answer: The horn draws out Echeyakee, the elusive white savannah cat. Sound it near the giant kodo bones northeast of the Crossroads, and the beast appears for a hunter to face.

faq.q: Where does the horn come from?
faq.answer: Sergra Darkthorn, an orc huntress at the Crossroads in the Barrens, gives the horn to adventurers seeking to prove their subtlety and tracking skill.

faq.q: What does the name Echeyakee mean?
faq.answer: In Taur-ahe, the Tauren tongue, Echeyakee means “Whitemist.” The name honors the beast’s pale coat and his silent way of stalking through dry grasses undetected.

faq.q: Where do you blow the horn?
faq.answer: Sound the horn among the giant kodo ribs and skeletal remains behind the hills northeast of the Crossroads, where the white lion roams.

angles.text: As a hunter, you face Echeyakee in a legendary rite of passage, testing your senses against a predator renowned across the Barrens for near-flawless stealth.
As a tauren, you know Echeyakee’s hunt carries spiritual weight. Your people see his swift, painless kill as both mercy and the harsh necessity of death.
